inheritedValidation.scope: Reference lab and application are unchanged. Prior 43 reference tests, three reference controls, exact Python fixtures, 13-dependency inventory, isolated frozen install, typecheck and 229 app tests remain baseline evidence, not new local executions in this increment. The PR CI runs these applicable checks again.

newProcessKills: After observer challenge insert before time update/commit: no partial preparation persists.
After challenge commit before return: complete unbound context and sampled time persist.
After exact request write before time update/commit: original challenge remains unbound and unsaved-request acceptance rejects.
After request commit before return: exact request binding and time persist; different randomized proof cannot replace it.
After receipt/consumption write before commit: original pending request and sequence/time survive; exact receipt can be retried.
newStorageFailures: SQLITE_FULL during preparation time update: challenge insert and time roll back together.
SQLITE_FULL during request time update: exact request binding and time roll back together.
SQLITE_FULL during receipt/consumption update: sequence/time advance rolls back with acceptance.
PRAGMA query_only generates SQLITE_READONLY on acceptance; pending exact request and replay memory remain intact.
Separate connection writer lock generates SQLITE_BUSY at transaction entry; acceptance remains retryable.
Separate connection reader lock generates SQLITE_BUSY at COMMIT after all acceptance writes; explicit rollback preserves exact pending request and replay memory.
faultMethod: Shared helper extracted unchanged from recovery.test.mjs into fault-support.mjs. A named trigger ABORT first proves the selected write is reached. A temporary trigger then attempts less than 2 MiB under max_page_count to produce a real SQLite FULL error. No host disk exhaustion. Lock tests use 1ms timeouts on their own connections; ordinary 5-second timeout unchanged.
additionalInvariant: Retrying after a persistence fault at the original challenge deadline does not extend freshness. Old request remains saved and unconsumed; a fresh challenge is required.
newNegativeControls: Commit challenge insertion separately before the preparation clock update.
Commit request binding separately before its clock update.
Omit explicit rollback after a failed COMMIT, leaving uncommitted acceptance writes visible.

limitations: Same-author local research with public PS issuer test keys, plaintext databases and unqualified secret BigInt operations; unsuitable for real assets.
RFC primitive vector and Node/noble verification do not provide independent review of the composed state protocol or PS equations/transcripts.
State signatures prove what the pinned issuer reported; no issuer honesty, no supply/equivocation defense and no guaranteed unspent state after the snapshot.
Fresh observers, same/higher-sequence forks, restored observer backups and manipulated time/trust are not protected by the remembered sequence/time checks.
No trusted manifest distribution, key rotation/retirement, secure time source, HTTP transport, wallet authentication, image/file/vault adapter or hosted issuer.

SIGKILL is not power loss; prior page-limit/query_only tests do not qualify real disk, hardware or permission failures. Arbitrary IOERR, corruption, all boundaries, retention/availability and devices remain open.
Wallet bytes remain context only; walletAuthenticated false. Public showings expose linkable h and nullifier.
C2 local harness complete; C1/C3 partial; independent C4 review and C5/C6 integration/hosting remain open.

Five observer interruption hooks are inert by default. These tests do not cover all constructor/write boundaries, arbitrary IOERR/fsync failures or hardware durability. No transaction correction was required.
